p1.title: Passage 1
paras: The intensifying frequency and volatility of extreme weather events serve as the most visceral manifestation of anthropogenically driven climate change, breaking free from the abstract metrics of global temperature averages. Meteorological anomalies—ranging from stagnant atmospheric high-pressure systems that lock in catastrophic heatwaves to hyper-intensified marine deluges—are no longer statistically isolated deviations but systemic recalibrations of the earth's biosphere. This new climate paradigm exposes the deep fragility of global infrastructure, which was fundamentally engineered under the flawed assumption of environmental stationarity. Urban centers, coastal defenses, and agricultural heartlands are routinely overwhelmed by ecological forces that collapse legacy protective barriers. The economic cascading effects are equally destabilizing, as systemic crop failures trigger food insecurity while escalating property destruction threatens the solvency of global insurance markets. Humanity is caught in a high-stakes race against feedback loops, where melting permafrost and retreating ice caps reduce global albedo, locking in further thermal absorption. Mitigating this existential crisis demands a fundamental shift from reactive disaster response to deep, systemic climate resilience and decarbonization.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: On March 12, 1930, when the British still had a firm grip on India, Mahatma Gandhi and seventy-eight of his disciples strode out of the Sabarmati ashram towards the sea. In the twenty-four days that followed they walked two hundred miles, picking up more and more companions as village after village turned out to cheer the Mahatma and raise the new Indian flag. By the time they reached their destination, the seashore at Dandi, the group numbered several thousand. Earlier in March, Gandhi had sent a letter to the British viceroy protesting the Salt Act, which forbade Indians to make their own salt and left them dependent on a British monopoly for what is, in a tropical country, a necessity of life. The viceroy did not reply. To Gandhi this was the “opportunity of a lifetime.”

questions.q: The author uses the phrase "environmental stationarity" to describe:
opts: The belief that climate patterns stay stable and predictable over time.
Weather systems stuck over one region.
questions.why: Vocabulary in context: infrastructure was built on the 'flawed assumption' that the climate would not change. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: According to the text, a major threat to the global insurance market comes from:
questions.why: Detail: the fifth sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: What is the direct consequence of the reduction of "global albedo" mentioned in the passage?
opts: More heat absorbed by the earth, adding to warming.
questions.why: Detail: 'locking in further thermal absorption'. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: Based on the passage, extreme weather events should be viewed as:
opts: A systemic reorganisation of the earth's biosphere.
Proof that old climate models worked.
Isolated anomalies that will correct themselves.
questions.why: Detail: 'no longer statistically isolated deviations but systemic recalibrations'. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: The passage suggests that the best approach to modern climate risk is:
opts: Reactive disaster management with old barriers.
Decarbonization together with proactive, systemic resilience.
questions.why: Main idea: the last sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.why: Detail: 'In the twenty-four days that followed they walked two hundred miles'. (Replaces a garbled item in the original paper.) Passage: GPSC CBRT (Mamlatdar / Vigilance Officer), Jun 2025.

questions.q: Which is the correct order of events? (i) Gandhi leads 78 volunteers out of Sabarmati (ii) Gandhi writes to the viceroy (iii) Villagers join the march (iv) Several thousand reach Dandi
questions.why: Sequence: the letter was 'earlier in March', before the 12 March start. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Mamlatdar / Vigilance Officer), Jun 2025.

questions.q: Why did Gandhi call the viceroy's silence "the opportunity of a lifetime"?
opts: It made the viceroy his ally
It let him begin the Salt Satyagraha with public sympathy
It allowed him to leave India
It ended British rule at once
questions.why: Inference: the unanswered letter justified the march. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Mamlatdar / Vigilance Officer), Jun 2025.

questions.q: Choose the correct inverted structure:
opts: Not only did he finish the report, but he also presented it.
Not only he did finish the report, but also he presented it.
Not only he finished the report, but he also presented it.
Not only did he finished the report, but he also presented it.
questions.why: 'Not only' at the start: did + subject + base verb. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Spot the error: “The patient, along with his relatives, were waiting outside.”
questions.why: Phrases like 'along with' do not change the subject ('patient'): 'was waiting'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Select the correct indirect speech: She asked me, “Where do you live?”
opts: She asked me where I lived.
She asked me where did I live.
She asked me where do I live.
She asked me that where I lived.
questions.why: Reported questions use statement word order and no 'that'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct tense: “This is the third time he ______ late this week.”
questions.why: 'This is the first/second/third time' takes the present perfect. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Identify the clause type: “The nurse who attended me was very kind.”
questions.why: 'Who attended me' describes the noun 'nurse'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: PM-KISAN was continued for 2026-27 to 2030-31 with an outlay of about:
questions.why: PM-KISAN gives ₹6,000 a year to farmer families. Aug 2026.

questions.why: Announced Sep 2026.

questions.q: Who was named interim President of FIDE in July 2026?
questions.why: FIDE is the world chess federation.

questions.q: World Tourism Day is observed on:
questions.why: 25 January is National Tourism Day in India.

questions.q: Cotigao Wildlife Sanctuary is in which taluka?
questions.why: Now in Kushavati district.

questions.q: The Indian Coast Guard was raised in:
questions.why: It works under the Ministry of Defence.

questions.q: In October 2026, Tata Motors raised its offer for the acquisition of:
Who won the Nobel Prize in Literature 2026?
questions.why: The Canadian poet and essayist. Oct 2026.

questions.q: India's largest state by area is:
questions.why: Goa is the smallest.

questions.q: Find the next number in the series: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, ?
questions.why: These are the prime numbers in order. The next prime after 13 is 17.

questions.q: Find the next term in the series: AZ, BY, CX, DW, ?
questions.why: The first letter moves forward and the second moves backward: E and V.

questions.q: In a certain code each letter is replaced by the letter in the same position counted from the other end of the alphabet, so GOA becomes TLZ. How is INDIA written?
questions.why: I-R, N-M, D-W, I-R, A-Z.

questions.q: Find the odd one out.
questions.why: 121, 144 and 169 are the squares of 11, 12 and 13. 200 is not a perfect square.

questions.q: Q is the brother of P. R is the daughter of P. S is the sister of Q. T is the mother of S. How is T related to R?
questions.why: P, Q and S are siblings and T is their mother. R is P's daughter, so T is R's grandmother.

questions.q: A clock shows 4:30. It is placed so that the minute hand points east. In which direction does the hour hand point?
questions.why: At 4:30 the minute hand is at 6. If 6 points east, then 3 points north, and the hour hand, between 4 and 5, points north-east.

questions.q: If A = 1, B = 2, …, Z = 26, what is the sum of the letters in EXAMINATION?
questions.why: 5+24+1+13+9+14+1+20+9+15+14 = 125, which is not listed. GPSC's printed key said 150; the sum is 125, so E. GPSC CBRT, Jun 2025.

questions.q: The sum of the present ages of a father and son is 60. Six years ago the father was five times as old as the son. What will the son's age be after 6 years?
questions.why: f + s = 60 and f − 6 = 5(s − 6), so s = 14 now and 20 in six years. GPSC CBRT, Jun 2025.

questions.q: Employees and managers are in the ratio 7 : 3. 70% of employees and 30% of managers eat in the canteen. What per cent of the workforce eats in the canteen?
The HCF of two numbers is 12 and their LCM is 924. If one number is 132, find the other.
questions.why: Product = HCF × LCM: 12 × 924 ÷ 132 = 84. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2025.

questions.q: Who wrote 'Keynotes and Characteristics with Comparisons of some of the Leading Remedies of the Materia Medica'?
questions.why: Henry Clay Allen wrote the Keynotes. Nash wrote 'Leaders in Homoeopathic Therapeutics'.

questions.q: Which remedy is regarded as the chronic of Aconite?
questions.why: Sulphur is the chronic of Aconite: it continues the work of Aconite in deeper, slower states.

questions.q: Want of grit, offensive foot sweat and a tendency to expel foreign bodies such as splinters indicate:
questions.why: Silicea: lack of stamina and confidence, offensive sweat of the feet, and expulsion of foreign bodies from the tissues.

questions.q: A mild, yielding, weepy patient who is thirstless, has changeable symptoms and is better in the open air needs:
questions.why: Pulsatilla: gentle, tearful, seeks consolation, thirstless, wandering symptoms, worse in a warm room and better in open air.

questions.q: Craving for salt, aggravation at about 10 a.m. and aggravation from consolation point to:
questions.why: Natrum mur.: salt craving, 10 to 11 a.m. aggravation, and dislike of consolation, which makes the patient worse.

questions.q: Intolerable urging to urinate, with burning, cutting pains before, during and after urination, calls for:
questions.why: Cantharis: violent burning and cutting pain with constant urging, passing urine drop by drop.

questions.q: Extreme sensitiveness to cold air and to touch, splinter-like pains and a tendency to suppuration indicate:
questions.why: Hepar sulph.: oversensitive to cold and touch, splinter-like pains, and inflammation that tends to suppurate.

questions.q: Warts and condylomata, the fixed idea that the body is brittle like glass, and ill effects of vaccination point to:
questions.why: Thuja: the chief antisycotic, with warty growths, the glass delusion and complaints following vaccination.

questions.q: Stinging, burning pains with oedematous swelling, thirstlessness and relief from cold applications indicate:
questions.why: Apis: bee-sting pains, puffy swelling, no thirst, worse from heat and better from cold.

questions.q: Painlessness and stupor with stertorous breathing, and constipation with no urging at all, are characteristic of:
questions.why: Opium: insensibility, deep stupor with snoring breathing, and complete inactivity of the bowels.

questions.q: Comparative Materia Medica is mainly concerned with:
opts: studying related remedies side by side to tell them apart
questions.why: Comparative study sets similar remedies against each other, by modalities and characteristics, so the right one can be chosen.

questions.q: A fat, fair, flabby child whose head sweats profusely during sleep, with slow dentition and a craving for eggs, needs:
questions.why: Calcarea carb.: leucophlegmatic constitution, head sweat in sleep, late teething and walking, desire for eggs.

questions.q: In the centesimal scale, the ratio of drug to vehicle at each step is:
questions.why: One part of the previous potency to 99 parts of vehicle, a dilution of 1 in 100 at each step.

questions.q: The decimal scale of potentisation was introduced by:
questions.why: Hering introduced the decimal (1 in 10) scale. Hahnemann used the centesimal and, later, the LM scale.

questions.q: In the 6th edition of the Organon, the 50 millesimal (LM) method of preparation is described in:
questions.why: §270 gives the LM method. §269 deals with potentisation in general and §128 with provings in the 30th potency.

questions.q: The Korsakovian method of potentisation uses:
opts: a single vial, emptied and refilled at each step
a new vial at each step
a continuous flow of water through the vial
questions.why: Korsakoff's method uses one vial throughout; the Hahnemannian method uses a fresh vial for each potency.

questions.q: Trituration is the method used to prepare potencies of:
opts: insoluble substances such as metals and minerals
questions.why: Insoluble substances are ground with sugar of milk until they can be dissolved and potentised further.

questions.q: The usual vehicle for trituration is:
questions.why: Sugar of milk (Saccharum lactis) is hard, neutral and suits grinding.

questions.q: In homoeopathic pharmacy, the symbol Φ denotes:
questions.why: Φ marks the mother tincture, the starting preparation of a plant drug.

questions.q: Which of the following is a sarcode?
questions.why: Sarcodes come from healthy tissues or secretions, such as Thyroidinum. Psorinum and Medorrhinum are nosodes; X-ray is an imponderable.

questions.q: The Homoeopathic Pharmacopoeia Laboratory of the Government of India is located at:
questions.why: The Homoeopathic Pharmacopoeia Laboratory, set up in 1975, is at Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh.

questions.q: Good manufacturing practice for homoeopathic medicines is laid down in which Schedule of the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules?
questions.why: Schedule M-I sets the GMP requirements for homoeopathic medicines.

questions.q: In a prescription, the symbol Rx forms the:
questions.why: The superscription is Rx (recipe, take). The inscription names the medicine, the subscription instructs the dispenser and the signatura instructs the patient.

questions.q: The abbreviation 'h.s.' on a prescription means:
questions.why: 'h.s.' (hora somni) means at bedtime, which is not among options A to D.

questions.q: Beyond about which centesimal potency is it unlikely that even one molecule of the original substance remains?
questions.why: At 12C the dilution is 10 to the power -24, beyond Avogadro's number (about 6 x 10 to the power 23).
